newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GELDERSE PAPIER RETURNS TO PROFIT IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: GELDERSE PAPIER RETURNS TO PROFIT IN 1996.

text.p: Dutch paper maker Gelderse Papiergroep NV said on Wednesday it expected a 1996 net profit of 1.7 million guilders compared with a total loss of 30.3 million in 1995.

"Improved margins (in the second 1996 half) compared to the first, as well as lower fixed costs due to restructuring have resulted in a net profit from ordinary operations of some 5.6 million guilders in the second half," Gelderse said.
In the first 1996 half the company posted a loss of 3.7 million guilders.
In August the company, which is 70 percent owned by NV Koninklijke KNP BT , said it expected second-half profits would be sufficient to offset the first half loss.

The company said it had not booked any extraordinary items in 1996. In 1995 Gelderse posted an extraordinary loss of 17.0 million guilders after tax, on top of a 13.3 million guilder loss from ordinary operations.
Gelderse said that it expected first half profits in 1997 to at least equal those of the second half of 1996.
"Based on recent performance and assuming a limited rise in cellulose prices, we expect results in the first half of 1997 to at least equal those of the 1996 second half," Gelderse said.
The company said it would publish final 1996 figures on March 12.
